title: "Design Lab: Hotel Inventory and Reservations"
---

# Design Lab: Hotel Inventory and Reservations

Build a Go reservation API for one hotel and room type before adding search. The invariant is explicit: for every stay date, confirmed reservations plus live holds cannot exceed capacity. A cached “rooms available” result cannot enforce this invariant.

## Model dates and state

Use the hotel's calendar dates with a half-open stay `[check_in, check_out)`. Store inventory rows keyed by `(hotel_id, room_type, stay_date)` with capacity and allocated count. A reservation stores guest, stay range, quantity, idempotency key, state, and hold expiry.

Use `POST /holds`, `POST /holds/{id}/confirm`, and `POST /reservations/{id}/cancel`. The first milestone allocates a hold without contacting a real payment provider. Repeat requests with one key return the same reservation; changing the payload under that key is a conflict.

## Prevent overselling transactionally

Lock all inventory rows for the stay in ascending date order using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`. Validate capacity for every date before incrementing any allocation. Insert the hold and commit the transaction. Never reserve each night in its own transaction.

A conditional update can enforce the local row bound:

```sql
UPDATE inventory
SET allocated = allocated + $1
WHERE hotel_id = $2 AND room_type = $3 AND stay_date = $4
  AND allocated + $1 <= capacity;
```

The Go code must check `RowsAffected() == 1` and roll back the entire stay if any night fails. Validate positive quantities and database constraints independently. [PostgreSQL row locking](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/explicit-locking.html) explains the lock behavior used here.

Use `sql.Tx` with request context, `defer tx.Rollback()`, checked errors, and a checked `Commit()`. A commit error can leave the caller uncertain; resolve retries by the stored idempotency key. For serialization failures, retry the complete transaction with a bounded budget, not just the failed statement.

## Expiry and payment boundary

Confirmation and hold-expiry workers must lock the same hold row before deciding its transition. Release inventory exactly once when a hold becomes expired or canceled. A late payment success after expiry needs an explicit refund or recovery path; it cannot blindly resurrect inventory already sold to another guest.

Do not hold database locks while waiting for an external payment API. Persist state, perform the external step, and reconcile through the [payment design lab](15-payment-system.qmd). Availability caches remain advisory and can lag actual inventory.

## Evidence

Race 100 Go clients for one remaining room over two nights. Assert exactly one successful hold and no negative availability. Test a missing inventory date, duplicate confirmation, expiry racing confirmation, cancellation replay, and a database failure on the second night. Query inventory after every scenario and compare it with active reservation rows. Measure lock waits and deadlocks before considering partitioning across hotels.
